_comment: Provenance + UI-drift contracts for OpenELIS user-manual sections. Each section maps to the manual doc it backs, the live instance + routes it documents, and the on-load UI anchors (headings / labels / buttons) the manual relies on. The drift check (tests/docs/drift.check.spec.ts) visits each route and asserts the anchors still exist; missing anchors => the manual section may be stale. 'capturedVersion' is the OpenELIS version the screenshots were taken against.

sections.title: Analyzer file import
sections.notes: Linked to page 1047265314 'Import analyzer results from a file' (Taib, 2 February 2026; re-homed under Set up an analyzer on 15 September 2026). Its fourteen figures predate 3.2.2.0. Route anchors re-verified on testing.openelis-global.org 3.2.2.0 on 2026-09-22. Gap: the page's 'Where' is Main menu -> Analyzers -> Analyzer Results, and on testing there is no Analyzer Results entry in the Analyzers menu - /AnalyzerResults redirects to /analyzers. The surviving file-import screen there is Generic Sample -> Import, which is the route anchored here, so the page's step text needs re-checking against it.

sections.title: Admin — Compliance Standards & Holding-Time
sections.notes: Re-pointed to testing 2026-09-22. DECISION 2026-09-23 (Casey): the manual documents the new Test Catalogue Management editor ALWAYS; the legacy /MasterListsPage/TestModifyEntry screen is no longer documented and its route has been removed. The two anchors this section used to carry moved as follows, both verified cold on testing 3.2.2.0 on 2026-09-23: 'QC Acceptance Thresholds' -> the 'QC Targets' editor section; 'SOP Max Holding Time' -> 'Maximum storage duration' + 'Duration unit' in the 'Sample Storage' editor section. Both sit on a CLINICAL test, so the environmental-sample-type gap that blocked the legacy screen on testing no longer applies. CAVEAT ON THE TEST ID: /MasterListsPage/TestCatalogEditor/{id}/{section} needs a concrete id; 6 is Albumin(Urines) on testing and is instance-specific - these two routes will route-error on any other instance. The durable fix is a resolver token in drift.check.spec.ts alongside {{ORDER_IN_PROGRESS}} (e.g. {{ANY_TEST}} resolved from the catalog list), which has not been added. STILL TO DO: published page 1421148161 Step 5 and Figure 3 still tell the reader to open Modify tests and set 'SOP Max Holding Time (minutes)' under 'QC Acceptance Thresholds' - that single step now SPLITS across two editor sections (QC Targets, Sample Storage) and needs rewriting plus a re-shot figure. capturedVersion left at 3.2.1.10 until that lands. PNGDEMO CROSS-CHECK 2026-09-23 (driven on screen; base stays testing per Casey). pngdemo runs a Vite dev server and needs ~50s to mount - it is not down, just slow; an earlier read gave up too early. On pngdemo 3.2.2.0 the Test Catalogue Editor has 15 sections, read off the left nav: basic-info, sample-results, methods, ranges, storage, panels, labels, terminology, reagents, analyzers, alerts, accreditation, reflex-calc, localization, display-order. TWO DIFFERENCES FROM TESTING, both confirmed on screen: (1) 'qc-targets' NO LONGER EXISTS - /TestCatalogEditor/{id}/qc-targets redirects to /basic-info, so the qc-targets route registered here will become a routeError as soon as pngdemo's build reaches testing; where QC targets moved to is UNRESOLVED (the new 'accreditation' section is unrelated - it reads 'test is not accredited by any body / Manage accrediting bodies and expiry dates' - and the qc/controlLots + qc/dashboard modules are the likely new home). (2) 'accreditation' is new and absent on testing. The storage section is IDENTICAL on both: all seven anchors present on pngdemo test 696 Acanthamoeba sp-PCR-Air(Water). ALSO: pngdemo HAS the environmental catalog (Water and Air sample types; 611 configuration issues vs testing's 61), so the environmental-sample-type gap recorded above is a testing seed-data gap, not a product gap. QC TARGETS RESOLVED 2026-09-23 (driven on pngdemo): they left the test editor for a new top-level 'Quality Assurance' menu (which on testing is still the older 'Non-Conform / EQA Tests / EQA Management' set). Quality Assurance > Statistical QC holds QA Overview (/qa/overview), QC Dashboard (/qa/qc/dashboard), QC Alerts (/qa/qc/alerts), QC Lot Management (/qa/qc/control-lots), Rule Configuration (/qa/qc/rule-config), Reagent QC (/qa/qc/reagent-qc) and Analyzer Manual QC (/qa/qc/manual-qc). Targets are now LOT-first, not test-first: /qa/qc/control-lots is 'Control Lots - Manage QC control lots for Westgard rule evaluation' with columns Lot Number / Control Material / Manufacturer / Control Level / Status / Calculation Method / Expiration Date, and the New Control Lot form (which redirects to /analyzers/qc/control-lots/new) carries Lot Number, Control Material, Control Level, Expiration Date, Analyzer, Test, Status and a 'Statistics Configuration' block of CALCULATION METHOD (e.g. Manufacturer Fixed) / MEAN / STANDARD DEVIATION - the statistical equivalent of the editor's 'Expected value' and 'Uncertainty (+-)'. So the editor's per-test three-level QC Targets table is replaced by per-control-lot mean/SD. NOTE the nav link /qa/qc/control-lots and the form route /analyzers/qc/control-lots/new are different route families - check for redirects before anchoring either.

sections.note: 2026-09-23: section repointed from testing to analyzers.openelis-global.org, and all four figures re-captured there. Reason: testing has no Analyzer Bridge (/analyzers/types shows 'Analyzer types could not be loaded - Check the Analyzer Bridge connection'; rest/analyzer-types returns 502 'Bridge URL is not configured'), so no analyzer can be registered and this workflow cannot run there at all - its anchors were passing only because empty shell pages render. The analyzers host runs the workflow fully (13 analyzers, a live rule set). CAVEAT - the analyzers host is a build BEHIND testing: it shows Analyzers List columns 'Test Units'/'Type' where testing shows 'Lab Units'/'Analyzer type', and its Rule Configuration page still renders the pre-OGC-1224 'Analyzers > Quality Control Dashboard > Rule Configuration' title with no real h1. Step 1 prose and the anchors follow the analyzers host. When that host picks up the newer build, expect 'Test Units' to fail here - that is the signal to re-capture and restore the Lab Units / Analyzer type wording. HISTORY - the 19 Sep failure on '/analyzers :: Analyzer List' was a true positive: the page-hierarchy title 'Analyzer List' (i18n analyzer.page.hierarchy.list) was rendered at the 2026-09-02 capture and has since been removed from AnalyzersList on both hosts. OPERATIONAL - this section now only runs when the drift check is invoked with BASE=https://analyzers.openelis-global.org; a testing-only weekly run will skip it silently.

sections.title: Import a test catalog from CSV
sections.notes: Anchors read off figure 01 (the empty import page) and verified on testing.openelis-global.org 3.2.2.0 on 2026-09-22. 'Catalog area' is deliberately NOT anchored: it is the file-table column header and only exists after a file has been added, so anchoring it would fail on every load. 'Nothing is waiting for a decision.' is likewise not anchored, since the queue is shared and fills up; the 'Needs your decision' heading is always rendered. The apply hint and the red save-failure notification are also not anchored: each exists in only one state. OGC-1228 (Apply wrote nothing) is fixed and Done; the defect panels were removed from the page on 2026-09-24, Step 6 rewritten, figures 02 and 04 re-captured and figure 06 (populated What was loaded) added. Because the version string did not change across the fix, use buildMarkers, not capturedVersion, to tell a pre-fix build from a fixed one. Driven on 2026-09-24: a pending decision does not block Apply (the dependent row is skipped and the name stays queued), and a file error keeps Apply closed after preview. Figure 05 re-captured 2026-09-24 with realistic names (Haematology Unit, tests-cphl-haematology.csv). The save-failure notification in Step 6 has not been driven live; Casey accepted it without the unverified flag on 2026-09-24.

buildMarkers.note: The version string reads 3.2.2.0 on both the broken and the fixed build, so it cannot tell them apart. Check the main frontend bundle (/assets/index-*.js) for these strings instead. The bundle hash itself is not stable: index-DiLvlcZ5.js on 2026-09-22, index-BB_UyTgo.js on 2026-09-24, both fixed.
